title: Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly
abstract: arXiv:2610.31778v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Long horizon agentic tasks are now pushing LLM agents past their context window. To continue the task, the agent scaffold has to free up the context window, a process known as context compaction. Compaction is generally lossy by design: agents can silently lose task constraints, instructions, or their reasoning behind earlier decisions. Although compaction is a standard component of coding agent scaffolds, it has not been studied systematically with frontier models on realistic, long horizon agentic tasks. Previous work evaluate smaller open weight models on toy or synthetic trajectories. We fix the agent scaffold (OpenCode), implement five compaction strategies inside it, and evaluate three frontier models on three long horizon benchmarks (PaperBench, ProgramBench, PostTrainBench). translated_title: 基准测试出人意料地对上下文压缩友好
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.31778v1 公告类型： cross 摘要：长时程智能体任务目前正在将大语言模型（LLM）智能体推向超出其上下文窗口的范围。为了继续执行任务，智能体框架必须释放上下文窗口空间，这一过程被称为上下文压缩。压缩在设计上通常是有损的：智能体可能会悄悄丢失任务约束、指令，或者其早期决策背后的推理依据。尽管压缩已是编程智能体框架中的标准组件，但此前尚未有研究针对前沿模型在真实的长时程智能体任务上对压缩进行系统性研究。以往的工作仅在玩具型或合成的轨迹上评估较小的开源权重模型。我们固定了智能体框架，在其中实现了五种压缩策略，并在三个长时程基准上评估了三个前沿模型。对于两个具备100万上下文的模型，压缩阈值对任务性能没有可测量的影响，而对于上下文窗口最小的GPT-5.3-Codex……
tldr: 该论文首次在固定的智能体框架内实现五种上下文压缩策略，并在三个长时程基准上系统评估三个前沿模型，发现基准任务对有损压缩出人意料地友好——对百万级上下文模型而言，压缩阈值几乎不影响任务性能。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically evaluates five context compaction strategies within a fixed agent scaffold across three long-horizon benchmarks with frontier models, revealing that benchmarks are surprisingly compaction-friendly—compaction thresholds have no measurable impact on task performance for 1M-context models.
